### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7abf97ca5fcadb360b0ca8e4ec73f9cb59e3e227` — the merge of head `b779b7f25e652b22bb791c46a6e58c52ec183c37` into base `2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7abf97ca5fcadb360b0ca8e4ec73f9cb59e3e227 && git checkout 7abf97ca5fcadb360b0ca8e4ec73f9cb59e3e227
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12 b779b7f25e652b22bb791c46a6e58c52ec183c37 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12 && git merge --no-ff b779b7f25e652b22bb791c46a6e58c52ec183c37

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2c96e0dfc9297ba791c8acb6484ebe678dfd7d12
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6509c8617c1a6cfd03f1c5869ed967621a38c3ee`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/cross-object-negative-orphan.test.ts, .changeset/33792-cross-object-orphan-native.md, content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx + packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/cross-object-where.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/filter-normalizer.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-lowering.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/filter-normalizer-not-null-safe.test.ts
Security-touching: no

### ① Derived judgments

- Right: on the native SQL strategy, outside `$not`, a detail row with no parent (empty relation, or a dangling reference) is no longer selected by a cross-object leaf lowered to `notSet`, `empty` or `notContains`. That covers `$ne` a value, `$nin` and `$notContains` (through the `notSet` escape arm rule 3 of `filter-lowering.ts` lays around them), `$null: true`, `$eq: null`, `$empty: true`, and also `$exists: false` (same `notSet` leaf; not named in the changeset). The wrapped clause reads `("HOP"."id" IS NOT NULL AND CLAUSE)`; the last hop's alias comes from `resolvePathHops`, the resolver `qualifyAndRegisterJoin` reads, so two hops read `"order__customer"."id"`.
- Right: positive leaves (`equals`, `in`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `icontains`), `set`, `notEmpty`, `notEquals` and `notIn` take no conjunct, so their statements are byte-unchanged. A leaf on a base column or an SQL expression gets `null` from `joinedParentKey` and is unchanged. The diff touches no engine-strategy file. A parent that exists with a NULL field still satisfies the leaf.
- Wrong, M1: "nothing else moves" does not hold under `$not`. `compileFilterNode` wraps a null-satisfied joined leaf wherever it sits, including inside a `not` node, where the guard inverts. `{ $not: { 'order.status': { $null: true } } }` was `NOT ("order"."status" IS NULL)` (orphan FALSE, not selected) and is now `NOT (("order"."id" IS NOT NULL AND "order"."status" IS NULL))` (orphan TRUE, selected). Same for `$eq: null`, `$empty: true`, `$exists: false` under `$not`, and for `$notContains` on a non-text or JSON-stored column under `$not` (both arms of the escape become FALSE for the orphan). `$not` over `$ne` a value or `$nin` does not move (UNKNOWN stays unselected). The PR body's acceptance note that a `$not` operand's leaves "are positive or `set`" is false: `nullGuardForFieldSpec` returns `none` for a total spec and leaves it as written, and `filter-normalizer-not-null-safe.test.ts` pins `NOT ("stage" IS NULL)` for `$not` over `$eq: null` and a joined member under `$not` on this strategy.
- Wrong, S1: the moved surface is wider than "`where`". The same `compileFilterNode` compiles a measure's own `filter` (the conditional aggregate) and the dataset's own `filter`, both of which `dashboards.mdx` says are evaluated only on the native path when they read a related field. Their totals move the same way; the changeset's BREAKING notice names `where` alone.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/service-analytics': patch` with `!` in the title, a BREAKING banner, FROM → TO, a one-line fix, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: this is the shape AGENTS.md on main prescribes for a non-protocol breaking change (`none` takes `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition). No schema key or export changes, so `Metadata-protocol: none` and the marker's reason are right. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` concluded success on this head.
- The level is not the problem; the declaration's content is. Per M1 the diff also widens (orphans newly selected under `$not` of a null-satisfied leaf), which `no (narrowing)` and the FROM → TO do not state, and per S1 the FROM → TO names one of three filter positions that move.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty; nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, stale depth text in `dashboards.mdx` (engine path "One relationship", two or more refused, while #33626 serves up to three): agreed that it is outside this card's surface and correctly not edited here. It is noted with no carrier; escalated to the seat to file it, since the page is now touched by this PR and still states the stale depth.
- Dev flag, `$not` over a cross-object leaf "unchanged by this PR": not accepted, see M1.
- Dev deviations (HTML comment lines in the PR body, commit trailers without a model name): process matters for the dispatching seat, no effect on the contract.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): held. The fix is one conjunct on the join the statement already carries; no id materialisation, no in-app filter, no second query.
- Check-runs on this head: every run concluded success or skipped (Test Core 8/8, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness). The gates do not see M1: the new test file has no `$not` case.

### ④ Design judgment

- The narrowing itself is declared semantics, not a new choice. `cross-object-where.ts` on main states "No parent, or one the caller cannot read, never matches, whatever the operator, `$ne` / `$nin` / `$null: true` included", and `dashboards.mdx` on main says the same for the engine path. So `$null: true` and `$empty: true` leaving the orphan out is the published reading (the leaf asks about a record the relation reaches), and no ruling is needed for it. The card's expected result and #33512's acceptance note agree.
- Outside `$not`, the native result matches that rule for every listed operator, one hop and multi-hop: each hop joins on the alias `id`, so the last hop's key is NULL exactly when the chain reached no row, and a line whose order exists with no customer is left out of a two-hop leaf as on the engine. A deleted parent is a dangling reference (the recycle bin captures the row elsewhere), so it is covered. An unreadable parent is unchanged: the joined object's read scope stays its own WHERE conjunct through `applyReadScope`, which does not pass through the changed code. The conjunct is plain SQL and portable across SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server; the `or`-absorb path restores params and joins as before.
- M1 (must-fix) — the guard is not polarity-aware. Under `$not` it turns a leaf that was TRUE for an orphan into FALSE, so the negation newly selects the orphan. That is a widening in a `no (narrowing)` change, on exactly the rows this card is about. It contradicts the changeset's "no such row is selected, whatever the operator" and the new docs sentence, and it is the outcome `cross-object-where.ts` gives as the reason the engine refuses `$not` ("negating the existential test admits every row whose parent is absent"). Repair: do not add the conjunct inside a `not` operand (thread the polarity through `compileFilterNode`), which keeps those statements byte-unchanged as the PR body claims, and pin it with a `$not` case over `$null: true` on a joined member. Keeping the new behaviour instead is a semantic choice the engine path has no answer for; it would need a maintainer ruling, a declaration in the changeset and a test.
- S1 (should-fix) — the changeset's BREAKING notice must name every position that moves: a measure's own `filter` and a dataset's own `filter` beside `where`.
- S2 (should-fix) — "not selected, whatever the operator" in the docs sentence and the changeset over-claims on the native path even after M1 is repaired. A positive leaf under `$not` compiles to `NOT (col IS NOT NULL AND col = v)` and selects the orphan (unchanged, and the engine refuses the shape). `$nin: []` folds to the TRUE constant in `fieldLeaves` and selects every row, where the engine path's nested form would leave the orphan out (read from the code, not run). State the exceptions or close them.
- N1 (nit) — "The same `$or` keeps such rows on both paths": `{ order: { $null: true } }` keeps a row with an empty relation, not one naming a record that no longer exists; the sentence's "such rows" covers both. The test's own title says it correctly.
- N2 (nit) — the changeset's operator list omits `$exists: false`, which lowers to the same `notSet` leaf and moves with `$null: true`.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A3-33792`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ASNY8Ywba8ySbMdWvra2vS`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Review — FAIL
Head-sha: `6509c8617c1a6cfd03f1c5869ed967621a38c3ee`

L1 ordinary ACCEPT read. The declaration is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, so the contract record is review#2's.

### M1 (must-fix): under `$not` the conjunct now selects orphans that were left out before

The Acceptance notes say "`$not` over a cross-object leaf is unchanged on the native path. Its operand's leaves are positive or `set`, so they take no conjunct". The shared lowering says otherwise.

In `packages/spec/src/data/filter-lowering.ts`, rule 3 (`guardNullPolarity` with `negated`, through `nullGuardForFieldSpec`) treats `$null`, `$empty` and a null `$eq` as already total, and leaves them alone inside a `$not` operand. It gives a negative-polarity leaf (`$ne`, `$nin`, `$notContains`) the `{ $or: [{ f: { $null: true } }, { f: spec }] }` escape. So a `$not` operand does reach `compileFilterNode` with `notSet`, `empty` and `notContains` leaves, and each now takes `("HOP"."id" IS NOT NULL AND …)`. That conjunct is two-valued FALSE for an orphan, so the enclosing `NOT` turns it TRUE.

These are the exact statement shapes, run on SQLite with the PR's fixture shape. `o3` exists with a NULL status, `l7` has an empty relation, and `l8` has a dangling relation.

| `where` on the native path | before (main) | at this head |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `{ $not: { 'order.status': { $null: true } } }` → `NOT ("order".status IS NULL)` | `l1, l2` | `l1, l2, l7, l8` (both orphans newly selected) |
| `{ 'order.status': { $null: false } }` (same meaning) | `l1, l2` | `l1, l2` |
| `{ $not: { 'order.status': { $ne: 'open' } } }` (escape arm under `NOT`) | `l1` | `l1` |

`$not` over `$eq: null`, `$empty: true` and `$notContains` compiles the same way, as a `notSet`, `empty` or `notContains` leaf directly under `NOT` or inside an escape `$or`, and moves the same way. So in this one class the PR widens: rows the native answer left out are now counted. It also breaks two things the PR states:
- `$not {$null: true}` and `$null: false` agreed before; they now disagree.
- `dashboards.mdx` now says such a row is "not selected, whatever the operator", which is untrue under `$not`.

No test covers `$not`. The new file's cases are all un-negated.

**Fix**, inside this PR's surface:
1. Make the conjunct keep an orphan UNKNOWN, not FALSE, so a `NOT` cannot flip it. For example, `(CLAUSE AND "HOP"."id" = "HOP"."id")` is UNKNOWN on a NULL key and TRUE otherwise. On the same fixture, `NOT (("order".status IS NULL AND "order".id = "order".id))` answers `l1, l2`, and the un-negated cases still leave the orphans out. A `negated` flag carried through `compileFilterNode` is another way.
2. Pin `$not` over `$null: true`, `$eq: null`, `$empty: true`, `$notContains` and `$ne`: no orphan is selected, and the `$not {$null: true}` answer equals `$null: false`. Native face only, since the engine refuses `negated`.
3. Correct the Acceptance note.

### Holds

1. **The un-negated rule.**
   - `NULL_SATISFIED_LEAF_OPERATORS` (`notSet`, `empty`, `notContains`) is the right set outside a `$not`. Every other compiled operator is UNKNOWN on a NULL, or `IS NOT NULL`, so a positive statement is byte-unchanged.
   - The conjunct is added only around a clause that bound, so `params` stays aligned.
   - `joinedParentKey` reads `resolvePathHops`, the same resolver the join uses, and returns `null` for a base column or an expression.
2. **The tests.** The new file runs a native face, an engine face (`nativeSql: false`) and the engine's nested-relation `find` over one engine on `driver-sql`. It covers two orphan kinds, a parent that exists with a NULL value, two hops, and a positive control. The red-first measurement on main's strategy shows only native-face failures (11 of 12), and the `notSet` ablation reds 10 of 12 as described.
3. **Declarations.** Changeset `@objectstack/service-analytics: patch` with `!`, a BREAKING FROM → TO, the ADR-0087 `not-required` marker, and a `$or` remedy for authors are all consistent with an un-negated narrowing. M1 makes `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` untrue for the `$not` class until it is fixed.
4. **Battery stance.** service-analytics is not a shared package under the 16:10Z rule, and the merge group runs the Dogfood shards.
5. **Check-runs on the head.** Latest run per check: 38 success, 15 skipped, none failed or pending. `mergeable_state` is clean.

The patch-id is `ff4f14f69c5867855785e20ddbc11263301e3045`. A delta at the fixed head will be read against this record.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1 delta) · Head-sha: b779b7f25e652b22bb791c46a6e58c52ec183c37 · 2026-11-16T11:24Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-B, on the final head declared in 6915011564. Delta against the L1 FAIL 6911858976 at `6509c861`: three linear commits (`f2b0b56f`, `85d43a40`, `b779b7f2`), 4 files, +102/−16. The L2 delta at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is review#1's.

### M1 — resolved

- **The conjunct.** `native-sql-strategy.ts` now emits `(CLAUSE AND "HOP"."id" = "HOP"."id")` in place of `("HOP"."id" IS NOT NULL AND CLAUSE)`. That is the fix the FAIL proposed. For an orphan the key is NULL, so the conjunct is UNKNOWN and the leaf is UNKNOWN, never FALSE. A single `NOT` then gives UNKNOWN, so the row is not selected, which matches main (where the leaf was TRUE and the `NOT` gave FALSE). Un-negated, UNKNOWN selects what FALSE selects. I worked the two combinator shapes through Kleene tables, and both give the same answer as main:
  - `$not $or [$null, amount > 2000]`: orphans not selected;
  - `$not $and [$null, amount < 2000]`: `l8` selected, as on main.

  The SQL pins assert the new statement text, one hop and two.
- **Pins (fix item 2).** The new table has eight native `$not` cases, each held to its answer on `origin/main` `5a755791a9`: `$null: true`, `$eq: null`, `$empty: true`, `$notContains`, `$ne`, the `$or` and `$and` combinators, and two hops. A separate case pins `$not {$null: true}` = `$null: false`. The engine face is left out by design, because it refuses `negated`. The area's reading: these nine are green on main's source, red at `6509c861`, and green at head, and the `IS NOT NULL` ablation turns the same nine red.
